This '''list of Jewish mathematicians''' includes mathematicians and statisticians who are or were verifiably [[Jew]]ish or of Jewish descent. In 1933, when the [[Nazis]] rose to power in Germany, one-third of all mathematics professors in the country were Jewish, while Jews constituted less than one percent of the population.<ref name=haaretz>{{cite news |last=Aderet|first=Ofer|date=25 November 2011|title=Setting the Record Straight About Jewish Mathematicians in Nazi Germany|url=https://www.haaretz.com/1.5213290|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180628204921/https://www.haaretz.com/1.5213290|url-status=dead|archive-date=28 June 2018|work=[[Haaretz]]|access-date=2 July 2018}}</ref> Jewish mathematicians made major contributions throughout the 20th century and into the 21st, as is evidenced by their high representation among the winners of major [[List of mathematics awards|mathematics awards]]: 27% for the [[Fields Medal]], 30% for the [[Abel Prize]], and 40% for the [[Wolf Prize in Mathematics|Wolf Prize]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.jinfo.org/Mathematics.html|title=Jews in Mathematics|website=Jinfo.org|access-date=17 July 2018}}</ref>{{r|EJ|p=V13:678}}

* [[Israel Zamosz]] (c. 1700{{Snd}}1772), Talmudist and mathematician<ref>{{cite book|first=Gad|last=Freudenthal|chapter=Hebrew Medieval Science in Zamość ca. 1730: The Early Years of Rabbi Israel ben Moses Halevy of Zamość|title=Sepharad in Ashkenaz: Medieval Learning and Eighteenth-Century Enlightened Jewish Discourse|location=Amsterdam|editor1-first=Resianne|editor1-last=Fontaine|editor2-first=Andrea|editor2-last=Schatz|editor3-first=Irene|editor3-last=Zwiep|chapter-url=http://aleph.nli.org.il:80/F/?func=direct&doc_number=000468724&local_base=RMB01|year=2007|pages=25–67}}{{Dead link|date=May 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>
* [[Oscar Zariski]] (1899–1986), algebraic geometer; Cole Prize (1944), Wolf Prize (1981), Steele Prize (1981)<ref>{{Cite book | first=Carol | last = Parikh | title=The Unreal Life of Oscar Zariski | year=2014 | publisher= Academic Press | asin=B01DUEBQSC|page=1}}</ref><ref name=james/>
* [[Edouard Zeckendorf]] (1901–1983), number theory<ref>{{cite journal|first=Clark|last=Kimberling|author-link=Clark Kimberling|title=Edouard Zeckendorf|journal=Fibonacci Quarterly|volume=36|number=5|year=1998|pages=416–418|doi=10.1080/00150517.1998.12428899 |url=https://www.fq.math.ca/Scanned/36-5/kimberling.pdf}}</ref>
* [[Doron Zeilberger]] (born 1950), combinatorics<ref name=jinfo/>
* [[Efim Zelmanov]] (born 1955), mathematician; Fields Medal (1994)<ref name=jinfofields/>
* [[Tamar Ziegler]] (born 1971), ergodic theory and arithmetic combinatorics; Erdős Prize (2011)
* [[Leo Zippin]] (1905–1995), solved Hilbert's fifth problem{{Sfnm|1a1=O'Connor|1a2=Robertson|1loc=[http://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Zippin.html Leo Zippin]}}
* [[Abraham Ziv]] (1940–2013), number theory
* [[Benedict Zuckermann]] (1818–1891), mathematician and historian{{r|EJ|p=V21:678}}
